body.statement: Let \(\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\) contain the measurable rectangles \(\mathcal I_N\) satisfying \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\Pr_P\{\mu(P)\in\mathcal I_N\}\ge1-\alpha\). For every sequence of nonempty shells on which the legal same-shell deformation property posed in Open-ended Question 2 holds uniformly, \(c_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\le\inf_{\mathcal I_N\in\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N)\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\). For every nonempty shell, without the deformation premise, the profile-recentered inversion in \(\operatorname{def:moment-inversion}\) is uniformly honest and attains the upper inequality. Its full-box fallback occurs only on \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\), so for all sufficiently large \(N\) its expected contribution is zero and hence \(o\{(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\), uniformly because \(s_N\le1\).
body.justification: Profile recentering makes the nonlinear feasible set nonempty, a calibrated data-driven moment radius gives uniform coverage, and the lower width remains conditional on legal same-shell alternatives.
body.gap: Andrews and Cheng establish generic identification-robust inversion, and Zhu establishes weak-factor honesty costs; neither provides a total finite-moment inversion rule, a simultaneous moment-ball guarantee, or the \(s_N\)-specific missing-mean modulus for this cohort system.
body.consumer: The result provides simultaneous uncertainty bands for all missing untreated means in the Veneto wage application and in interactive-fixed-effect event studies without relying on pointwise Wald linearization.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\vartheta_0\) be the primitive parameter of a true \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\). The conditional moment bound implies \(\|m_c\|\leq B\) and \(\sigma_c\leq B\), so \(\vartheta_0\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\). Direct evaluation of conditional first and second moments under the rank-two outcome equation, loading-error orthogonality, and spherical errors gives
\[
g(\vartheta_0)=\theta(P). \tag{1}
\]
Put \(E_N=\|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\|_{\mathsf m}\). On the robust-ball event \(E_N\leq\widehat\rho_N\), the profiled distance satisfies \(d_N\leq E_N\), and hence
\[
\|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}=E_N
\leq\widehat\rho_N\leq d_N+\widehat\rho_N.
\]
Thus \(\vartheta_0\in\mathcal C_N\), and the enclosing rectangle contains \(\mu(P)\). The coverage assertion in \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) proves uniform level-\((1-\alpha)\) honesty for \(N\geq2k_\alpha\). For smaller \(N\), \(|\mu_{ct}|\leq B\) and the returned box \([-B,B]^{CT}\) covers with probability one.

For width, compactness of \(\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\) and continuity of \(g\) make the profiled minimum attainable and \(\mathcal C_N\) nonempty and compact. Its coordinate extrema are measurable: they are limits of extrema over deterministic finite \(1/j\)-nets after enlarging the continuous constraint by \(1/j\). For any \(\vartheta,\widetilde\vartheta\in\mathcal C_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}
&\leq2(d_N+\widehat\rho_N)\\
&\leq2(E_N+\widehat\rho_N),
\end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
where the last inequality uses the feasible true point in the definition of \(d_N\), without requiring the coverage event. Applying \(\operatorname{lem:observed-moment-inverse-modulus}\) to (2), the maximal target diameter of \(\mathcal C_N\) is at most
\[
K\min\!\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\}. \tag{3}
\]
The enclosing rectangle has maximal half-width no larger than half this diameter. Since \(x\mapsto\min(1,x)\) is concave and increasing, \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) and (3) give
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N)
\leq K\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\mathbb E_P(E_N+\widehat\rho_N)}{s_N}\right\}
\leq C_\alpha r_N. \tag{4}
\]
When \(N<2k_\alpha\), the width is bounded and \(r_N\geq(2k_\alpha)^{-1/2}\), so increasing \(C_\alpha\) proves (4) for all \(N\). The fallback event is deterministically empty once \(N\geq2k_\alpha\), proving the stated zero and little-oh assertions.

For the lower bound, apply \(\operatorname{lem:two-point-decision-lower-bounds}\) with \(\Delta\geq c_\alpha r_N\) and \(\kappa=(1-2\alpha)^2/8\). Then \(\sqrt{\kappa/2}=(1-2\alpha)/4\), and every honest rectangle has worst-case expected width at least
\[
\frac{3(1-2\alpha)}4\min\{1,c_\alpha r_N/2\}\geq c_\alpha' r_N.
\]
Taking the infimum over honest rectangles completes the proof.
